risk_if_not_implemented: Without Periodic Review of Exceptions, security, compliance and resilience activities may lack direction, ownership and executive support, leaving required controls unperformed. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unaddressed Security / Compliance Exposure (R-GV-2), Uncontrolled Internal Security / Privacy Exposure (R-GV-4), Lack of oversight of internal controls (R-GV-6), Inability to Demonstrate Due Diligence / Due Care (R-GV-9), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Statutory / Regulatory / Contractual Change (MT-11), Conflict of Interest (COI) / Undue Influence / Insider Misconduct (MT-15).

compensating_control_1.name: Approved Configuration Deviations
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to document, assess and approve or deny deviations to secure baseline configurations.
compensating_control_1.justification: Approved Configuration Deviations (CFG-06) provides configuration hardening and change discipline that compensates for the absence of Periodic Review of Exceptions (GOV-04.3) by enforcing secure settings and trusted software sources to reduce inherent exposure. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Risk Monitoring
compensating_control_2.description:
Mechanisms exist to monitor risk as an integral part of the continuous monitoring strategy, including: 
(1) The effectiveness of security, compliance and resilience controls; 
(2) Changes to the organization's risk profile; and 
(3) Changes to Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that affect risk.
compensating_control_2.justification: Risk Monitoring (RSK-22) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of Periodic Review of Exceptions (GOV-04.3) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
